common_name: Mona Lisa Lily (Dwarf Pink-and-White Patio Asiatic Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Mona Lisa is a dwarf Asiatic lily bred for patio pots and small garden spaces.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants while the flowering stem reaches into sun. Mona Lisa is a compact, dwarf Asiatic lily bearing soft pink, upward-facing blooms edged in white, opening on notably short stems that need no staking and fit well in containers or the front of a border where taller lilies would overwhelm the space. It blooms in early summer and, unlike fragrant Oriental lilies, has almost no scent, making it a good choice near seating areas for gardeners sensitive to strong lily fragrance. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Journey's End Lily (Crimson-Pink White-Edged Oriental Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Journey's End is a late-summer-blooming Oriental lily with large, richly colored, recurved blooms.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Journey's End bears large, strongly fragrant, recurved blooms in deep crimson-pink broadly edged in white with darker spotting toward the throat, opening late in the Oriental lily season to extend summer color into early fall. Its tall, sturdy stems make an excellent, long-lasting cut flower, though the intense fragrance can be overwhelming in a small enclosed room. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Muscadet Lily (White with Raspberry-Speckled Center Oriental Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Muscadet is a compact Oriental lily well suited to containers.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Muscadet bears large, strongly fragrant, mostly white blooms flecked with raspberry-red speckling that concentrates toward the throat, a delicate freckled pattern that gives it a softer look than solid-colored Oriental lilies. Its relatively compact habit compared to taller Oriental cultivars makes it a good choice for containers or the middle of a mixed border. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Black Beauty Lily (Deep Red-Maroon Vigorous Reblooming Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Black Beauty is an exceptionally vigorous lily hybrid known for producing many flowers per stem and multiplying quickly.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Black Beauty bears deep red-maroon, recurved blooms with a narrow green throat and white margin, on tall, exceptionally vigorous stems that hold many more flower buds per stem than most lilies, giving it a dramatic, full presence in the border. It multiplies and spreads readily, forming substantial clumps over a few seasons where many other lily hybrids stay slow to increase. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Conca d'Or Lily (Tall Creamy Yellow Orienpet Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade; Conca d'Or is an Orienpet (Oriental-trumpet) hybrid combining trumpet-lily vigor with Oriental-lily flower form.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Conca d'Or is an Orienpet, a cross between Oriental and trumpet lilies that combines the trumpet parent's exceptional vigor and height with the large, fragrant, outward-facing blooms typical of Oriental lilies, opening creamy yellow with white edges and a gold-brushed throat on very tall, sturdy stems. Its size and toughness make it an imposing back-of-border presence and an excellent, long-lasting cut flower. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Enchantment Lily (Classic Upright Orange-Red Spotted Asiatic Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Enchantment, introduced in the 1940s, remains one of the most widely planted Asiatic lily cultivars ever released.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Introduced in the mid-20th century, Enchantment bears upright, unscented, bright orange-red blooms heavily spotted with maroon toward the throat, and its ease of growth, vigorous multiplying habit, and reliable early-summer bloom made it one of the best-selling lily cultivars of all time, still widely grown today. Its sturdy, upright flower form needs no staking under normal conditions. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Connecticut King Lily (Unspotted Golden-Yellow Asiatic Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Connecticut King is a classic, widely grown golden-yellow Asiatic lily.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Connecticut King bears clean, unspotted, upward-facing golden-yellow blooms with a glossy sheen, a pure, uncomplicated color that has kept it a garden and cut-flower favorite since its introduction, blooming reliably in early summer on sturdy stems that need no staking. Its lack of spotting sets it apart from many other Asiatic lily cultivars, giving it a cleaner, more modern look. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: African Queen Lily (Fragrant Apricot-Orange Trumpet Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; African Queen is a classic trumpet lily with purple-flushed buds opening into large fragrant apricot blooms.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. African Queen is a classic trumpet lily bearing large, intensely fragrant, apricot-orange trumpets that open from dramatic purple-flushed buds on tall, sturdy stems, a rich warm color and powerful scent that has made it a long-standing favorite for both garden borders and cut-flower use. Trumpet lilies tend to be more vigorous and tolerant of a range of soils than many Oriental hybrids. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.

common_name: Golden Splendor Lily (Fragrant Golden-Yellow Trumpet Lily)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Golden Splendor is a classic golden-yellow trumpet lily with a maroon-striped reverse to the petals.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, keeping the base of the plant shaded with mulch or companion plants. Golden Splendor bears large, intensely fragrant, golden-yellow trumpets marked with a maroon stripe down the reverse of each petal, opening on tall, vigorous stems that make a bold statement at the back of a summer border. Trumpet lilies like this one tend to be tougher and more tolerant of a range of soils than many Oriental hybrids, and its powerful fragrance carries well across an outdoor space. Leave the foliage in place after bloom until it yellows naturally, since it recharges the bulb for next year's flowers.
